summary.title: How to build a simple artificial neural network with Go
summary.one_liner: You learn the intuition and math behind neurons, sigmoid activations, gradient descent and backpropagation, then implement a small 3-layer feedforward network in Go using the Gonum matrix library.
keywords: how does machine learning learn from mistakes
takeaways: A neural network is a mathematical model that learns by iteratively reducing prediction error, similar to adjusting a configurable parameter.
Sigmoid activation adds non-linearity and has an easy derivative, which makes backpropagation practical.
Gradient descent with the chain rule computes weight updates for output layers, and backpropagation reuses those errors to update hidden layers.
A learning rate scales weight updates to avoid overshooting the minimum; bias neurons are optional.
The Go implementation uses Gonum's mat package with helper functions for dot product, apply, scale and add to build a 3-layer network with Predict and Train methods.
summary.summary: The article starts with an intuitive guessing-game example showing how a parameter can be tuned iteratively to reduce error, then relates this to biological neurons and artificial neurons with weights and sigmoid activations. It walks through the calculus of gradient descent, the chain rule, and backpropagation, including the learning rate and bias. The second half implements a simple 3-layer feedforward network in Go, using Gonum's mat package wrapped in helper functions, with Predict (forward propagation) and Train (forward plus backpropagation) methods. The full code is in the linked sausheong/gonn GitHub repository.
